title: How much survival pressure do you actually want in a farming game?
author: PhoenixShadowborn
selftext:
I've been building *Farmweaver*, a cosy pixel-art farming, exploration and light survival game (for iOS and Android), using Claude Code and one of the design decisions I've made is to leave out some of the more punishing survival mechanics.

I'm curious what other people think about these systems. Do you enjoy having to manage food and thirst? Energy systems that make you faint if you overdo things? Curfews that penalise you for staying out past midnight? Or combat where dying means dropping your items?

For Farmweaver, I've kept the exploration and progression but removed those penalties. You don't need to eat or drink to survive, there's no punishment for staying out all night and dying doesn't mean losing your belongings. I want survival to be part of the experience without it constantly getting in the way of exploring and building your farm.

I'm interested in where other people draw the line. Which of these mechanics genuinely add something to a farming game and which do you prefer to play without?

Thanks in advance.

If you're curious about Farmweaver, you can view more information here as well as participate in open testing: [https://idlespaceweaver.github.io/farmweaver.html](https://idlespaceweaver.github.io/farmweaver.html)

**AI disclosure:** Claude Code was used to assist with programming. The game's artwork is created by human artists. One of the interesting parts of using AI coding tools has been being able to experiment with mechanics and shape the game around the experience I want to create.

comments.author: e3e6
comments.body: how about giving a bonus instead of punishing. i.e. if you eat well you have a speed bonus insteyof if you don't eat you die

replies.author: PhoenixShadowborn
replies.body: Yeah, indeed. I think bonuses and buffs are the way to go.

comments.author: aura-32
comments.body: Food buffs are a good way to make eating feel like a choice instead of a chore, especially if different meals push you toward different playstyles. Good luck with it, I'd be curious how it turns out.

replies.author: PhoenixShadowborn
replies.body: Thanks. I'll certainly be back asking a few more questions. :)
